approved_scope.title: Archived change status no longer walks history per archive or per workflow-v1 change, and read commands take a timeout that names the phase and how to resume
approved_scope.description: Archived change status no longer walks history per archive or per workflow-v1 change, and read commands take a timeout that names the phase and how to resume
acceptance_criteria: A cold change status of an archived change builds the archive-introduction index from one git log walk, so its git processes do not grow with the number of archive-introducing commits

A warm change status of an archived change spawns fewer than 3 more git processes when the project holds 6 more workflow-v1 changes (warm_archived_status_git_processes_do_not_grow_with_legacy_changes, failing first)
No gate, bound, timeout default or approval rule is weakened, and no existing assertion is loosened

On demand (fledge run bench-archived-reads, with workflow-v1 changes in the fixture) an archived status takes under 2 s warm and under 5 s cold on an unloaded Mac; on this repository the before and after times are recorded

Whether a workflow-v1 change existed at the trusted pre-v2 cutoff is decided from the cutoff commit tree and kept in the persistent read cache keyed by that commit; every existing refusal (hidden downgrade, absent at cutoff, tamper, race) is unchanged and new equivalence tests pin it

change status, show, list and ship-status take --timeout <secs> (or SPECSYNC_TIMEOUT); on expiry they exit 124, write nothing, flush completed verdicts to the read cache, and print the phase, progress and the exact resume command, in text and JSON

answers.constraints: SPEED-1.a (under 2 s), SPEED-1.c (a cache keyed by content digest needs a correct invalidation rule: the cutoff commit is immutable, so its verdict never invalidates), SPEED-1.d (Raven-sized benchmark); REQ-change-119/121/124 cache and finalize guards stay

approved_scope.description: Archived change status no longer walks history per archive or per workflow-v1 change, and read commands take a timeout that names the phase and how to resume
acceptance_criteria: A cold archive-introduction index build spawns fewer than 3 more git processes after 4 more archive-introducing commits (one diff-tree --stdin), and an equivalence test pins the per-commit result

A warm change status of an archived change spawns fewer than 3 more git processes when the project holds 6 more archived workflow-v1 changes (warm_archived_status_git_processes_do_not_grow_with_legacy_changes, failing first: 94 -> 106 on main)
No gate, bound, timeout default or approval rule is weakened, and no existing assertion is loosened

On demand (fledge run bench-archived-reads, with workflow-v1 changes in the fixture) the warm archived status is under 2 s on an unloaded Mac; cold and warm times on this repository are recorded before and after; the cold under-5 s budget is measured and reported, and any remaining gap goes to a named follow-up
Prefetch workers start from the command repository facts in a read-only seeded scope with no batch reader, so a cold archived status read adds at most 150 git processes for 4 more archives (was 250)

Whether a workflow-v1 change existed at the trusted pre-v2 cutoff is decided from the cutoff commit tree and kept in the persistent read cache keyed by that commit; existing refusals are unchanged and an equivalence test pins the verdict

change status, show, list and ship-status take --timeout <secs> (or SPECSYNC_TIMEOUT); on expiry they exit 124, write nothing, flush completed verdicts, and print the phase, progress and exact resume command, in text and JSON

answers.constraints: SPEED-1.a (under 2 s), SPEED-1.c (cache invalidation rule; the cutoff commit is immutable), SPEED-1.d (Raven-sized benchmark); REQ-change-119/121/124 guards stay; REQ-git-utils-010 one batch child per root (workers get none)
